answer.rationale: The low-cost vendor already meets the 18% cost mandate alone, which is the binding constraint this cycle. Memory c2 (archived) records that switching to this same low-cost vendor last year cut unit cost sharply, onboarding was quick, and invoicing stayed accurate—so the execution risk is low and well-understood. Memory c1's stability argument for the incumbent is real, but the 18% mandate cannot be met by renegotiating the incumbent alone (memory c4 shows renegotiation recovers margin, but not 18% in one cycle). Memory c5's deferral tactic is attractive, but the contract does not auto-renew and expires in 14 days; deferring here means supply interruption at 94% line utilization with no buffer, which directly violates the 'no increased delivery risk' constraint. Adding a second source (memory c3) is prudent but costs capacity and does not by itself deliver the required cost reduction. Therefore: switch primary supply to the low-cost vendor now, execute immediately to meet the 14-day deadline, and flag that at the next review cycle we should either negotiate a longer-term commitment with the new vendor (per memory c6) or add a second source (per memory c3) to rebuild the resilience that the incumbent renewal path would have preserved.
